paras: The killing of George Johnson in Ensley was the fatal shooting of a Black drayman by Special Officer Williams, Ensley's sanitary inspector, on the morning of July 28, 1903, during a quarrel over a tax. Williams gave himself up, and the only report found presented his claim that Johnson had been about to strike him with a chair.
Williams held the title of special officer in Ensley and was employed as the town's sanitary inspector. Johnson, described in the dispatch as "a negro," worked as "a public drayman."

According to a Birmingham special dated July 28, Williams demanded a tax of Johnson, who refused to pay. A quarrel followed in which, the dispatch said, Johnson "became excited," drew a chair and attempted an assault. Williams then drew a pistol and fired twice. The first bullet struck Johnson under the left eye without penetrating the brain, and the second entered his body beneath the heart and killed him.

Williams surrendered himself after the shooting, and the dispatch noted that there were witnesses, none of them named. No report of an inquest, charge, grand jury action or trial appears in the coverage found.

The shooting reached print in a short Birmingham special published by the Montgomery Advertiser on July 29, 1903, on page 5. Its opening sentence stated as fact that Johnson "was about to strike the officer with a chair," and it referred to him as "the negro" in describing his wounds. The dispatch named no source for its version of the quarrel and quoted none of the witnesses it mentioned.
No coverage of the killing was found in the Black press, so no Black correspondent's or editor's version of the events is available.

reader.title: Killing of George Johnson in Ensley
bases: A special officer employed as Ensley's sanitary inspector shot and killed George Johnson while demanding a tax from him; no crowd or mob is mentioned (A1).
Only one report, a Birmingham special in the Montgomery Advertiser, was found; no Black-press or local Birmingham coverage turned up (A1).

accounts.label: Birmingham special dispatch (officer's version)
accounts.gist: Johnson refused to pay a tax Williams demanded, became excited in the quarrel, and drew a chair to strike the officer, whereupon Williams fired twice in what the dispatch presents as response to the assault.

quotes: Special Officer Williams of Ensley this morning shot and killed George Johnson, a negro, who was about to strike the officer with a chair.
He demanded tax of Johnson and the latter refused to pay. A quarrel ensued and Johnson became excited.
Williams gave himself up. Johnson was a public drayman There were witnesses to the affair.
